mappings.note: sets up a cubic volume equation and finds the radius as its positive root; root-finding from a factorisation (C-2.3-LO-1), with the mensuration model itself uncovered by any outcome
V(x) = x(x+5)(x+6) built from a description (CG-2), then x^3 + 11x^2 + 30x - 112 = 0 solved by extracting the factor x - 2 (C-2.3-LO-1)
the new bin volume is already in factored form (x+2)(x+3)(x+4) and the answer is the root of the resulting cubic; modelling half has no outcome
both parts are remainder-theorem evaluations of a quartic model at m = 6 and m = 10. No zeroes, no coefficient relations, no graph -- the remainder theorem has no outcome in this frame at all
profit function formed by subtraction, maximised by completing the square, then evaluated by the remainder theorem. Every step falls outside the six learning outcomes
compares a remainder-theorem evaluation of a degree-5 model against direct substitution; the outcome set has nothing on either
a single remainder-theorem evaluation of L(n) at n = 6; no zero is ever sought
subtracts two volume polynomials to model a remaining solid and evaluates it by the remainder theorem at two heights; modelling plus remainder theorem, no outcome
divides a cubic by a quadratic and interprets quotient and remainder as families and leftover funds -- the division algorithm, which this frame does not carry at any level
the base side is obtained by factorising V = 3y(y+3)^2 and matching against the volume formula (C-2.3-LO-1); the surface-area part is mensuration with no outcome

the frame area gives 2x^2 + 15x - 27 = 0, solved by splitting the middle term and reading the roots off the factors -- the factorised-form-to-roots outcome on an equation, which is what separates it from C-2.1-LO-1 (zeroes of a named polynomial)
break-even is P(x) = 0 solved by factorising into (x-330)(x-20) (C-2.3-LO-1); the maximum-profit part is a vertex question with no outcome
time to hit the ground is the positive root of -4t^2 + 16t + 20 = 0 by factorisation (C-2.3-LO-1); maximum height by completing the square has no outcome
V(x) factorised as (x+1)(x-2)(x+2) so the third dimension is read off the factors; the surface-area and evaluation parts fall outside every outcome
